ruling.recommended_action: Send to a human reviewer to determine whether the 09:49–09:56 segment (F3) was driven on Bedok Reservoir Road as agreed in F7/F8; if it was not, record the RD-1 breach and apply the RD-6 account flag on the driver's 2 prior upheld route disputes (F17). No fare adjustment is due on this fixed quote.
ruling.reasoning:
The record settles the physical detour: one off-route segment, F3 (09:49–09:56, 4.87 km driven where the optimal route covers 3.00 km, +1.87 km, up to 1064 m off route), which under RD-1 is a segment requiring review under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [F1][F3][RD-1]. The trace marks RD-4(a) as failed — no qualifying traffic incident on the replaced stretch [F14][RD-4], and a speed band alone does not exempt [F11][RD-4] — so the segment is not excused by RD-4.

On RD-5, the rider sent "Sure, go ahead." at 09:46 [F8] in reply to the driver's 09:45 proposal to "go round via Bedok Reservoir Road" [F7]; the rider's message is timestamped and precedes the segment start of 09:49 [F9][F3], so the "before you go" element is met. But the agreement is a SPECIFIC named-road authorisation, not a general route choice: F7 names Bedok Reservoir Road only [F7]. Under RD-5 the record must tie this segment to that road, and nothing does — no message places the car on it, F3 names no road for the driven path, and no other fact names it [F3][F7][F9][RD-5]. Nor does any fact place the segment elsewhere; F12 and F13 name roads elsewhere in the city without tying them to this segment [F12][F13], so the "elsewhere" branch is not made out either. The ground is therefore named_road_untied and the finding undetermined (G13), as the trace and the stipulation set it [F3][RD-5]. The driver's after-trip statement that the rider agreed [F10] is a claim, not rider consent (G11), and adds nothing [RD-5].

The undetermined finding is decisive here, because the trace states it decides the RD-6 account flag: the driver has 2 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so a non-exempt segment would make this a repeated breach [RD-6]. It changes no amount — the fare is a fixed RydeX quote of $35.91 [F6], the billed distance 17.0 km does not exceed the 17.0 km optimal route [F4], and F6 lists no ERP/toll, waiting fee or post-trip add-on, so RD-2's non-metered branch yields $0 and the RydeTAXI formula (1.87 × $23.91 ÷ 16.96 = $2.64) does not apply [F3][F6][RD-2]. Because the finding changes the flag, the case goes to a human reviewer rather than being auto-decided [RD-5]. No_action is not available: it would require a finding that the segment is exempt, and the record does not let me read the rider's named-road consent onto the segment actually driven [F3][F7][F8][RD-5].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, all chat messages (F7, F8) and the driver's statement (F10) in full. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is an ordinary route request and reply [F7][F8][F10]. safety_concern = none [SAFE-1].

Evidence: the chat is complete and timestamped [F9], the GPS segment is measured [F3], and the fare record is present [F6]; nothing needed for the ruling is missing. The one thing the record cannot settle is the meaning/coverage of the agreement, which is a reading the record itself does not resolve — that is an undetermined finding under RD-5/G13, not a missing record. evidence_status = sufficient.

segment_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message, 'Sure, go ahead.' at 09:46 [F8], timestamped [F9], replies to the driver's 09:45 proposal to 'go round via Bedok Reservoir Road' [F7] and so precedes the segment start of 09:49 [F3] — the RD-5 'before you go' element is met. But the consent is a specific named-road authorisation: it covers driving on Bedok Reservoir Road only, and under RD-5 the record must tie this segment to that road. Nothing does — the chat names no road for the driven path [F7][F8][F9], F3 carries no road name, and F12/F13 name other roads without tying them to this segment — while nothing places the segment elsewhere either. Timing alone cannot establish coverage (G13), so the scope of the agreement cannot be read onto the segment actually driven: finding undetermined under RD-5.

rejected_claims.reason: Correct that the ground is undetermined (named_road_untied, G13) [F3][F7][F8][RD-5], but the claim that this 'drives the outcome' so as to leave no_action unavailable only in the direction of a human review is right and is adopted; its premise that the case cannot be auto-decided is accepted, while its implication that no_action could follow a favourable reading is not — with the record untied, escalation is the only outcome available.

Accepted on the money: the fixed RydeX quote of $35.91 [F6], billed distance 17.0 km not exceeding the 17.0 km optimal route [F4], no surge [F5] and no toll/add-on in F6 mean RD-2's non-metered branch yields $0 [RD-2][FARE-1]. This is consistent with my ruling, but it does not dispose of the RD-6 flag, which the undetermined segment decides [F17][RD-6].

Rejected in its conclusion. F7 names Bedok Reservoir Road and F8 is a timely rider reply [F7][F8][F9], but RD-5 requires the record to tie the segment to that named road; no fact does [F3][F7][F8], so the finding is undetermined (G13), not exempt as D2 urges [RD-5].

Rejected as an excuse. F11's speed band 2 on the Pan Island Expressway ends at 09:49, exactly when the segment begins [F3][F11], and F14 records no incident anywhere near the route; RD-4(b) does not exempt a segment on its own and RD-4(a) is unmet [F14][RD-4]. The congestion evidence explains the driver's reason, not the segment.

Rejected in its conclusion that the matter closes as no_action. The absence of a refundable amount [F4][F6][RD-2] does not extinguish the RD-1 duty breach recorded in F3 [F3][RD-1], nor the RD-6 flag that follows a non-exempt segment given the driver's prior [F17][RD-6].

Rejected as deciding the case. The driver's profile [F17] may inform only the additional account action and cannot determine whether the segment is exempt; here it is precisely the RD-6 basis for review if the segment is held non-exempt [F17][RD-6].

Rejected as presently operative: RD-6 requires this case first to be established against the driver (refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) [RD-6], and because the only segment is undetermined [F3][RD-5], the flag is for the human reviewer to apply, not for this ruling; the rider's clean profile [F16] has no bearing on whether the segment was consented to.
